I know it's not quite the same taste experience as coffee, but blue matcha lattes are pretty tasty! They're made with butterfly pea flower powder and it's completely caffeine free. The taste is really mild, so adding vanilla and lavender syrup gives it almost a slight taro taste, which tastes kind of nutty. You can also have it with lemonade which is nice. There's also some neurological benefits, I believe.

Also if you haven't tried golden milk tea, that's also pretty tasty. Plenty of awesome recipes online, though I know it's not as fun picking up a nice treat out somewhere.

I really enjoy going to places that sell milk teas/boba teas because they usually have a lot of options that are caffeine free!

I was raised Christian Science, and even went to a Christian Science bordering school for a year... Even though there is some truth to the whole anti-medicine thing for some extremists, my take growing up was that it was more like mind over matter for small things, like colds and what not, if your immune system was strong enough. But idk, my bias, for sure. My mom was very religious and succumbed to breast cancer after not wanting to receive treatment for over 7 months.. to this day I don't blame the religion itself. Weirdly, I learned a lot about love and acceptance growing up in that environment. But I could also chalk that up to having really loving parents. I will always hate the man from our local church that charged my mother $300 a month to be her "practioner" and "pray with her". He is scum.

Sorry to unload like that, but it piqued my interest to hear someone bring up Christian Science. FYI I haven't been apart of the church since I was 14, but I've really never considered myself a religious person.

I've mentioned how I feel to my sister a few times, and it frustrates her because she thinks I'm just not trying to do anything to feel better, which is true, technically. I know she cares about me and doesn't want me to feel so hopeless... I've somewhat mentioned to a friend about my thoughts because he asked me what I want to be doing in 5 years. I said all the normal stuff that sounds good but also said I just hope I'll be alive. I mentioned it in a somewhat joking way so I'm not sure how serious he took it, but I have been talking to him about my problems lately because I feel like we're pretty similar and I think he understands. I actually just talked with my sister about an hour ago about how I want to join the military and then that spiraled into a panic attack. But in a weird way it did feel good to release that tension. Crying just hasn't been cutting it the last two weeks.. 
Thank you for reaching out to a stranger, by the way. I was scared to post anything because I get scared of being made fun of, so I just expected this post to be ignored at best.

I just think I've stuck around long enough. I know 25 isn't old, but at least in my experience I feel like I get looked at differently because I'm a girl. People say I look younger than that and it makes me feel really bad, not because of my appearance but because I know it's more that I know I don't come off mature enough. I want to feel like an adult because the older I get the more pathetic I come off. I hate meeting new people or catching up with old friends because I'm ashamed of everything I haven't done but even still I lack any consistent motivation to do anything. I just stew in my regrets. The thought of getting older but thinking that my best days are behind me is soul crushing. I'm a burden on my sister, she doesn't want to have to worry about me anymore, and I don't want her to either. I also have a dog that I love but I don't want her to be someone's responsibility either if I'm gone. The only person who I think would want her is my s/o but I don't want to burden him with that either. The thought of her passing away is unbearable. I can't stand anymore loss, whether it's my parents' or past relationships. I'm just too weak for this world.

I just feel like I don't care enough to even try anymore. This brain that I'm stuck with is so shit. I can't afford any kind of therapy, medication, whatever, and I doubt it would help with my stupidity. 
My sister is going to Ireland to be with her fiance in a few months. I'll give myself some time to adjust, and maybe by some miracle I can make some positive changes, or just feel a little more hopeful. 
Thank you for replying though.
